rows.en: July, A.D. 1999. The object that fell onto South Ataria Island, a lone Pacific isle,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'gigantic' dropped (row 2 says giant battleship); 'lone isle in the Pacific' -> 'lone Pacific isle'

rows.en: was a giant space battleship, built with technology far beyond Earth's science.
The battleship brought a technological revolution through OverTechnology,
rows.notes: review: refit/rebalance: 'existence' cut; 'but at the same time' moved to row 4 as 'but it also'

rows.en: but it also pointed to an unknown threat from extraterrestrial life.
rows.notes: review: rebalance: takes 'but ... also' from row 3

rows.en: A.D. 2000. To counter the threat that was sure to come from space,
humanity founded the "U.N. Government," a body above all nations.
However, no small number of factions opposed it,
and they banded together as the Anti-U.N. Forces,
rows.notes: Anti-U.N. Forces per brief mapping of the alliance term; source has no quote marks here (unlike row 52).

rows.en: sparking the conflict that would later be called the "Unification Wars."
The war dragged on, finally ending in 2007. Meanwhile, the giant battleship
rows.notes: review: refit: tighter wording

rows.en: was under constant repair, to be reborn as a U.N. Forces battleship.
rows.notes: review: refit: tighter wording

rows.en: After so many years of war, the threat from space that had started it all
was all but forgotten. Yet the hour of destiny was close at hand...
A.D. 2040. In search of new places to live, humanity
had sent many large-scale colony fleets out into space.
Numerous planets had been discovered and developed into colony worlds,
and an age had come when many a generation called one of them home.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'no longer rare for a generation' -> 'many a generation'

rows.en: Drawn into the first interstellar war in history 30 years earlier,
humanity had narrowly escaped extinction by wielding the power of "culture,"
rows.notes: review: refit: 'with ... as its weapon' -> 'by wielding'

rows.en: made peace with the Zentradi forces, and founded the New U.N. Government.
But the end of the war did not simply mean the arrival of peace.
rows.notes: review: Mistranslated structure: source says it was not so simple that war's end equalled peace; current English compares the end of the war with the arrival of peace.

rows.en: It began with postwar reconstruction, then quelling some Zentradi remnants,
rows.notes: review: Dropped qualifier: source says a portion of the Zentradi remnants, not all of them. | review: refit: 'the suppression of some of the' -> 'quelling some'

rows.en: and went as far as bolstering defenses against unknown threats yet to come.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'stretched all the way to' -> 'went as far as'

rows.en: The New U.N. Forces were still absolutely indispensable,
rows.notes: New U.N. Forces per brief; glossary organizations.json lists this term as 'New U.N. Spacy'.

rows.en: and the buildup of new fighting strength went on as well...
rows.notes: Same term as row 24. Ends with ellipsis as in the source.

rows.en: A.D. 2045. The 37th colony fleet, which had left Earth seven years earlier,
built around Macross 7, the seventh ship of the New Macross class,
rows.notes: review: rebalance: 'carrying over a million citizens' moved to row 28

rows.en: carried over a million citizens through space, seeking a new planet to settle.
rows.notes: review: rebalance: takes the citizens clause from row 27 as the main verb

rows.en: The fleet's commander, who was also captain of the space carrier Battle 7,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'also served as' -> 'was also'

rows.en: was Maximilian Jenius, the genius pilot of Space War I.
Meanwhile, City 7, Macross 7's residential area, was governed by Mayor Milia,
rows.notes: review: rebalance: 'once feared even within the Zentradi forces' moved to row 32

rows.en: once feared even within the Zentradi forces as "Milia the Ace."
rows.notes: Name moved to the end of the sentence to match the row cut; 'Milia the Ace' is the quoted epithet. | review: rebalance: takes the epithet clause from row 31

rows.en: She was also Max's wife, wed to him in wartime in the first interstellar marriage.
rows.notes: review: refit: tighter wording

rows.en: Led by these two former aces, the Macross 7 fleet sailed on in peace,
but that a battle with the fearsome Varauta Army lay in wait for them
was something not a single person had foreseen...
A.D. 2059, 49 years after the end of humanity's first interstellar war.
rows.notes: Source has the year at the end of the sentence; written as 'A.D. 2059' since it opens the Frontier prologue, matching the other prologues.

rows.en: The 25th giant colony fleet to set out, the "Macross Frontier,"
was sailing on toward the center of the galaxy.
The living areas inside the ship recreated the same environment as Earth's,
and over 10 million people went about their peaceful daily lives.
But at the end of that tranquil voyage,
a fierce battle against unknown space creatures lay in wait,
and almost none of the citizens had any idea...
The giant battleship that fell on South Ataria Island in the late 20th century
rows.notes: review: refit: 'space' dropped; 'at the end of' -> 'in the late'

rows.en: made humanity aware of extraterrestrial life and the threat it posed, while
rows.notes: review: refit: 'that ... existed' compressed

rows.en: it also brought about a technological revolution through OverTechnology.
But the impact the giant battleship had on Earth did not stop there.
To counter those unknown threats,
the "U.N. Government" was founded, a body above all nations, while
factions around the world that rejected the U.N. Government's monopoly
rows.notes: review: rebalance: 'on OverTechnology' moved to row 52; 'refused to accept' -> 'rejected'

rows.en: on OverTechnology organized themselves into the "Anti-U.N. Forces."
rows.notes: review: rebalance: takes 'on OverTechnology' from row 51

rows.en: The "U.N. Forces" and the "Anti-U.N. Forces." Their conflict grew fiercer
rows.notes: review: refit: 'The conflict between the two sides' -> 'Their conflict'

rows.en: and at last sparked the struggle later called the "Unification Wars."
rows.notes: review: refit: 'led to the outbreak of' -> 'sparked'

rows.en: Amid the still-raging Unification Wars, on Mayan Island, a lone southern isle,
rows.notes: review: refit: tighter wording

rows.en: readings were picked up that, like the crashed battleship, seemed alien-made,
rows.notes: Source says an object showing alien-seeming readings was discovered; split as readings (56) / object found (57) to keep the row cut. | review: refit: 'seemed to be the work of alien life' -> 'seemed alien-made'; 'giant' dropped

rows.en: and the object giving them off was discovered.
rows.notes: See row 56.

rows.en: Over this mysterious object, which must have been on Earth since antiquity,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'ancient times' -> 'antiquity'

rows.en: the "U.N. Forces" and "Anti-U.N. Forces" began a secret but fierce struggle...
rows.notes: review: refit: second 'the' dropped

rows.en: The battleship brought a technological revolution through OverTechnology,
rows.notes: DYRL prologue begins here without its own year line; rows 60-61 repeat rows 3-4 and use the same wording. | review: refit/rebalance: same as row 3; 'but at the same time' moved to row 61

rows.en: but it also pointed to an unknown threat from extraterrestrial life.
rows.notes: review: rebalance: same as row 4

rows.en: To counter the threat that was sure to come from space,
the U.N. Government then repaired the giant battleship that crashed to Earth
rows.notes: Source opens with an 'and then/and so' connector that follows on from rows 60-61; rendered as 'then'. | review: refit: 'had crashed' -> 'crashed'

rows.en: and remade it as the U.N. Forces battleship "Macross."
As fate would have it, the threat from space came on the Macross's launch day.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'the very day of the ... launch ceremony' -> 'launch day'

rows.en: Having sensed the Macross, an alien battleship appeared near Earth,
rows.notes: review: rebalance: 'and hostilities with it' moved to row 67

rows.en: and hostilities with it suddenly broke out.
rows.notes: review: rebalance: takes clause from row 66

rows.en: To escape the overwhelming enemy attack, the Macross risked a fold.
With 50,000 citizens aboard, it jumped to the outer solar system, near Uranus.
rows.notes: Source literally says 'far beyond the solar system' but names Uranus; rendered 'far reaches of the solar system'. | review: refit: 'still' dropped; 'far reaches of the solar system' -> 'outer solar system'

rows.en: The Macross began its journey home to Earth,
but it could not shake off the relentless pursuit of the alien enemy.
And today, once again, the aliens launched their attack...
Zola, a planet on the edge of the Milky Way.
Home to the Zolans since ancient times, it was a quiet, utterly ordinary planet
rows.notes: Zolans (people of Zola) is not a glossary entry; derived from 'Zolan' used in glossary descriptions. | review: term now in glossary | review: refit: 'utterly unremarkable, peaceful' -> 'quiet, utterly ordinary'

rows.en: where the Zolans lived easygoing, tranquil lives.
rows.notes: Zolans, see row 74. | review: term now in glossary

rows.en: But Zola had one thing that set it apart.
Mysterious giant life-forms that at times appeared nearby: the "Galaxy Whales."
rows.notes: review: refit: 'sometimes appeared in the space around the planet' -> 'at times appeared nearby'

rows.en: Long revered and feared as gods on Zola, the Galaxy Whales
were in fact thought to be energy beings with a plant-like structure.
But once it was known that the whales could power high-performance ships,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'ever since it became known', 'be used to power', 'spaceships' compressed
